title: Scottish Music 1
description: Revise Scottish Music concepts introduced up to National 5, including instruments and features used in related Celtic music.

items.prompt: Name the broad national musical tradition encompassing the folk songs, dances and instrumental music of Scotland.
An opening musical phrase is followed by a responding phrase.
A processional or military-style piece with a strong, regular walking pulse, usually organised in two or four beats per bar. Name this type of music.
A fast Scottish dance in simple duple or quadruple time, characterised by flowing, even running quavers. Name the dance.
A dance in simple triple time with three beats in each bar.
A soloist or group performs without any supporting accompaniment. What term describes the absence of accompaniment?
A free-reed instrument sounded by opening and closing bellows.
A six-string guitar with a hollow body that resonates and amplifies the vibrating strings without electricity.
A wind instrument with an air-filled bag, a chanter for the melody and one or more drone pipes that sustain continuous notes.
A collection of drums and cymbals played by one performer using sticks, brushes and foot pedals.
A violin used in traditional or folk music, especially Scottish music.
Name the general ensemble category for a group performing folk traditions, often with acoustic instruments and singers.
